about: Harvested descriptions for AOP numbered trails. AOP identifies trails by NUMBER; names below are onX-contributor-applied labels (NOT the park's nomenclature) except #96 which is the park's own 2015 blog wording. Raw zone only — do NOT promote to publish.* without source_register rows + license clearance (onX text is onX-copyright; #96 is AOP-copyright-via-Wayback).
difficulty_legend: Park map: green circle = Easy, blue square = Moderate, black triangle = Difficult. onX technical rating (TR) 1-10 shown where known.

trails.name: Launchpad
trails.description: AOP 1 - Launchpad begins with a fine dirt-filled trail with a slight uphill climb. Once you make it to Area 51, there is lots of loose rock that makes you feel like you're driving on a cobblestone road.

trails.name: Convergence
trails.description: AOP's trail 2 - Convergence is an easy route that peels off of trail 1 - Launch Pad and curves around towards the buggy side of the park. Trail 2 is a convergence point for water that runs off the mountain and feeds into the nearby Battle Creek.

trails.name: Major Tom
trails.description: 3 - Major Tom is an excellent trail on the more casual side that can be underestimated. At the same time, Major Tom is a more accessible trail that can sometimes lead to complacency for a starter vehicle or one with less ground clearance.

trails.name: Lifeform
trails.description: AOP Trail 5 - Lifeform is a peaceful uphill climbing connector trail. Trail 5 features small rocks, exposed roots, and curving bends that bring you out to Trail 3.

trails.name: Descension
trails.description: AOP trail 6 - Descension is a mild downhill trail that starts off as a dirt flat, and ends with a deeply rutted and eroded section. The bottom half rut also has an exposed tree root.

trails.name: Ascension
trails.description: AOP 7 - Ascension can be quite a slippery slope when wet. When the trail is dry it is a fun hill climb for all vehicle types.

trails.name: Little Dipper
trails.description: AOP trail 9 - Little Dipper is a full loop trail that connects back to itself, but also connects to a few other more difficult trails. Trail 9 - Little Dipper is mostly flat throughout with little to no obstacles.

trails.name: Ground Control
trails.description: AOP trail 11 - Ground Control is like a child's roller coaster - slightly uphill then back down over and over. Trail 11 - Ground Control has concentrated clusters of rock, however none are difficult to traverse.

Trail 96 is a Blue, or moderate difficulty trail. This trail is a short loop that contains many rock and ledge obstacles that challenge drivers to negotiate angles and clearance. This trail is passable by modified Jeeps and Trucks. (Video shot at Trailfest 2015.)
trails.source_note: Park's own 2015 BigCommerce blog post — the only per-trail writeup the park ever published. Refers to the trail by number only, no name.
